risks.issue: executor_identity does not exist yet, and no Pool method or module function resolves an executor field to provider/model. The spec never gives its signature, return shape, or how 'claude:opus' and 'claude:success_floor' map, so 'resolve as specified' in the criteria can't be checked. 'claude:success_floor' also looks like a models-table key, not an executor id. The round-1 failures were only 'test not defined', so the executor is effectively rewriting the whole feature from a vague spec.

eligible_executors currently makes no Pool.pick calls. Adding a claude-row headroom check needs Pool.pick('execute'), which reads cooldowns and utilization and can roll the window. The spec doesn't say whether pick runs once before the loop or per row. Only the 'at most once' and 'zero calls for codex-only' bounds are given, so the check must be lazy: skipped when no enabled row has a claude provider, and memoised per call. A claude row's max_parallel is checked against ex.running, and nothing shown in the codebase increments that for Claude executions. The 'excluded at max_parallel' criterion would pass in tests while the guard does nothing in production.

codex_available and pick_executor go through eligible_executors and then filter on provider == 'codex'. A cooling or empty claude row must not mask a codex row. test_codex_available_true_beside_heavier_claude_row has no stated setup, such as which row wins ranking or scorecard cost. The scorecard path in pick_executor can pick the claude row and return False even though a codex row is eligible. The spec should say codex_available checks eligible codex rows and doesn't depend on the ranked pick.

review_tier(t) and _security_review_tier(t) take only the task. The 'pool_config called at most once when cfg=None, zero when passed' criterion needs a cfg parameter threaded through both functions and through _open_reviews. That loop calls the tier functions once per review, so without threading it loads config n times. The spec doesn't say to add cfg=None as a defaulted trailing arg, and existing callers and tests (test_daemon.py around lines 2454-2473) call the one-arg form. Nothing says how a None executor makes 'no pool_config call'.

Fail-closed behaviour is underspecified. 'Other tier plus the stderr line' has no defined 'other' when the executor's model is unknown, and no exact stderr text to assert on. The 'other tier' also has to be relative to the tier being chosen: review_tier compares against the model, and _security_review_tier compares against SECURITY_REVIEW_TIER. Silently falling back to the default sonnet on a lookup error would reintroduce self-review, and the spec should say how that case resolves. The model-to-tier mapping (substring match versus exact model id) is also unstated. It has to preserve the legacy claude:<tier> string behaviour when there is no models table.

Resolving identity in the daemon by constructing Pool(cfg) is heavy and has side effects. The constructor loads persisted state and runs _sync_legacy_codex, which mutates state, and it is built once per review decision. The spec should require a pure cfg-only lookup, not a Pool instance. That would also give the load-once guarantee cheaply, and daemon.py and pool.py stay decoupled.

All tests live in the same scope as the code, and the 'hard-coded expected values' criteria are the only guard against tautological asserts. Mocking Pool.pick to count calls must patch the class attribute, and the tests must build cfgs in memory. Otherwise Pool() reads the real PERSIST file and pool.toml, and the shared _harness root gets polluted.

suggested_spec_changes: State the exact signature and return value of executor_identity. Suggested: a cfg-only function or Pool method returning (provider, model) or None, with the row lookup order and the meaning of 'claude:<tier>' legacy strings versus 'claude:success_floor'.

State that eligible_executors calls self.pick('execute') at most once, lazily, and only when a candidate row has provider 'claude'. Codex-only configs must never call pick. Define how a claude row's running count is sourced, or drop 'excluded at max_parallel' for claude rows.
State that codex_available is true iff any eligible codex-provider row exists. Don't derive it from the single ranked pick, so a heavier or cheaper claude row can't hide it.
Add cfg=None as the last parameter of review_tier and _security_review_tier and have _open_reviews load config once and pass it down. Keep the one-arg call form working.

Define the fail-closed result precisely. On any exception while resolving, return the tier that differs from the one being chosen (opus for review_tier's default, _other_tier(SECURITY_REVIEW_TIER) for security). Emit one exact stderr line, with the wording given so the test can assert it.

Define precedence between the executor-row model lookup and the legacy claude:<tier> string. With no models table the legacy string path must stay byte-identical. None, codex, unknown and modelless executors must return the default tier without touching pool_config.

Require all tests to be unittest.TestCase methods with in-memory cfgs and mock.patch.object(Pool, 'pick'). Give the rollback as a git revert of the T-1347 fix-round commit, since the four files are the whole blast radius.
